slides.text:
A loop repeats code. Rust has three: `loop`, `while` and `for`.

This module starts with `for`, the one you will use the most.
`for` takes each value of a range in turn and runs its block once for each of them.
A range stops **before** its end: `0..3` gives 0, 1 and 2. Write `0..=3` to include the 3.

exercises.title: Repeat with for
exercises.guide: Inside `main`, loop **three times** and print the counter.

chunks.guide:
Every Rust program starts at `main`.

- `fn` declares a function
- the braces `{ }` hold its body

Type it, following the ghost text.

`for` repeats a block.

`0..3` counts from **0** up to **3**, not including 3.
`println!` prints a line. `{i}` puts the value of `i` in the text.
